question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Her explanation was so convoluted that it left everyone __confused.__
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"scratching their heads"** means to be puzzled or confused about something. (असमंजस में होना)

 
 
• **Example:** The students were **scratching their heads** trying to solve the tricky math problem.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "Her explanation was so convoluted that it left everyone confused," the idiom "scratching their heads" perfectly fits as it describes people being perplexed due to the explanation. (असमंजस के कारण)

**​**Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Biting the bullet** (गंभीर स्थिति को सहन करना): To face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage.

 
 
• **Example:** She decided to **bite the bullet** and confront her boss about the unfair treatment.
 
 
 
• **Turning a blind eye** (जानबूझकर अनदेखा करना): To ignore something intentionally.
 
 
• **Example:** The manager **turned a blind eye** to the employee’s minor mistakes to maintain harmony in the team.
 
 
 
• **Stealing the show** (सबका ध्यान आकर्षित करना): To attract the most attention or admiration in a performance or event.
 
 
• **Example:** The young dancer **stole the show** with her breathtaking performance.
 
 

33:Td57,

The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e., **play his cards right**.
